# LPE Project

> The Law and Political Economy Project is an intellectual network exploring how law shapes economic power, inequality, and democratic governance through scholarly research, education, and community organizing.

The LPE Project brings together legal scholars, economists, and activists to challenge neoliberal frameworks and develop progressive alternatives for understanding and reforming economic systems. The project operates through research, teaching, student engagement, and public scholarship.

## Key Topics

- Law and Political Economy
- Neoliberalism
- Antitrust and Competition Policy
- Labor Law and Employment
- Economic Inequality
- Constitutional Politics
- Indigenous Sovereignty
- Market Definition
- Legal Realism
- Economic Power
- Democratic Reform
- Progressive Traditions
- Social Control
- Regulatory Policy
- Economic Justice

## Foundation & Mission

- [LPE Project - The Law and Political Economy Project](https://lpeproject.org): Homepage introducing the Law and Political Economy Project network
- [About - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/about): About page describing LPE Project mission, team, and scholarly approach
- [Toward a Manifesto - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/lpe-manifesto): Foundational LPE manifesto by Kapczynski, Grewal, and Britton-Purdy outlining the intellectual framework
- [Our Team - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/our-team): LPE Project leadership and staff directory including founders

## Learning & Education

- [LPE 101 - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/lpe-101): Introductory lecture series with video and readings on LPE frameworks
- [Learn - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/learn): Educational resources including video lectures and course syllabi
- [Anti-monopoly and Regulated Industries - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/amri-academy): AMRI Summer Academy on antitrust law and economic power
- [Archives: Syllabi - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/syllabi): Archive of course syllabi on law and political economy topics
- [Archives: Primers - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/primers): Primers on neoliberalism, legal realism, and progressive traditions

## Scholarship & Commentary

- [Law and Political Economy Blog - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/blog): Blog covering law, political economy, and resource allocation
- [The Political Economy of Settler Backlash - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/blog/the-political-economy-of-settler-backlash): Ben Gerstein on indigenous sovereignty and regulatory backlash
- [The Market Definition Trap - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/blog/the-market-definition-trap): Hal Singer on antitrust market definition and competitive harm
- [What Would a Russell Vought of the Left Look Like? - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/blog/what-would-a-russell-vought-of-the-left-look-like): Beau Baumann on constitutional politics and democratic reform
- [LPE in the News - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/in-the-news): Media coverage of LPE Project research on vaccines and policy

## Community & Engagement

- [Engage - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/engage): Engagement hub for LPE student groups and community organizing
- [Labor, Social Control, and Counterpower - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/labor-social-control-and-counterpower): Conference on labor law, social control, and counterpower at Harvard

## Optional

- [Archives: LPE events - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/events): Archive of past LPE events including NYC-focused night school series
- [Weekly Roundup: March 20 - LPE Project](https://lpeproject.org/blog/weekly-roundup-march-20): Weekly roundup on antitrust, labor policy, and indigenous rights
